additions.reason: The Torah uses extensive bechina language to describe ben (son): ben is the bechina of da'at ha-rav that remains in the world after the tzaddik's passing; ben is the bechina of the upper level of perception (hasagat dari ma'alah); ben equals talmid ('ben ve-talmid kullu chad'). The son/student cluster is the most prominent conceptual domain in the first two-thirds of the Torah and is entirely absent from the current dataset. Ben is explicitly called bechina of 'ayin lo ra'atah' perception and of the Moshe-level tzaddik's legacy.
additions.source_quote: וּבֶאֱמֶת בֵּן וְתַלְמִיד הוּא כֻּלּוֹ חַד

additions.reason: The talmid (student) is the bechina of dari mata (lower-world perception), the one who sees 'melo khal ha-aretz kevodo'. The Torah states explicitly: 'ha-talmid hu bechina't ben' and 've-talmid hu bechina't dari mata'. The entire section of the Torah from paragraphs dalet through yod is built on the bechina relationship between ben and talmid.

The sage/wise man of the generation (chakham ha-dor) is explicitly called bechina of Moshe: 'u-Moshe Rabenu hu bechina't chakham ha-dor'. The chakham ha-dor is the one whose makifim (upper lights) are the highest; he illuminates both ben and talmid levels. This node connects the Moshe cluster to the ben/talmid cluster.
additions.source_quote: מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּנוּ... הוּא בְּחִינַת חָכָם הַדּוֹר, שֶׁהוּא מֵאִיר בְּבֵן וְתַלְמִיד

additions.reason: Makifim (surrounding/enveloping lights of intellect) are the central technical concept of this Torah. The Torah explicitly states: 'zeh bechina't shefah ha-keter, ki keter hu bechina't makif'. Makifim are also called bechina of me'od (very/extreme), bechina of the hidden good ('mah rav tuvekha asher tzafanta'). They are the spiritual overflow that enters the chakham's mind when he transmits his inner knowledge to his students.
additions.source_quote: וְזֶה בְּחִינַת שֶׁפַע הַכֶּתֶר, כִּי כֶּתֶר הוּא בְּחִינַת מַקִּיף

additions.reason: Keter (the crown/highest sefirah) is explicitly called bechina of makif (surrounding): 'keter hu bechina't makif, kemo she-katuv: kitru et Binyamin'. The shefa ha-keter (overflow of keter) is what the chakham ha-dor receives when he teaches his students. This is a core bechina in the Torah.
additions.source_quote: כֶּתֶר הוּא בְּחִינַת מַקִּיף, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: כִּתְּרוּ אֶת בִּנְיָמִין

additions.reason: Yovel (the jubilee) is explicitly called bechina of klaliut ben ve-talmid (the totality of son and student): 'yovel hu otiyot: ve-khal banayikh limudei H', de-haynu klaliut ben ve-talmid'. Yovel/cherut (freedom) is the source from which malkhut receives parnasah. This is a direct bechina statement in the Torah.
additions.source_quote: יוֹבֵל הוּא אוֹתִיּוֹת: וְכָל בָּנַיִךְ לִמּוּדֵי יְיָ, דְּהַיְנוּ כְּלָלִיּוּת בֵּן וְתַלְמִיד

additions.reason: Kohen (the priest) is called bechina of klaliut ben ve-talmid: 'kohen hu bechina't klaliut ben ve-talmid, ki be-kohen ne'emar: le-horot et bnei Yisrael — le-horot lashon hora'ah, zeh bechina't talmid. Gam le-horot lashon heiryon, bechina't ben'. This is an explicit double bechina.
additions.source_quote: גַּם כֹּהֵן הוּא בְּחִינַת כְּלָלִיּוּת בֵּן וְתַלְמִיד

additions.reason: Malkhut (kingship) is explicitly called bechina of Livyatan (the primordial sea-creature): 'Livyatan zeh bechina't malkhut'. Malkhut is also the source of yirah (fear/awe) and the channel through which parnasah (sustenance) flows. The entire second half of this Torah is built around malkhut receiving parnasah from the yadayim (hands) in the sea of chokhmah.

Livyatan is explicitly called bechina of malkhut: 'Livyatan zeh bechina't malkhut, kemo she-katuv: Livyatan nachash baria'ch... u-ferush Rashi: malkhut'. This is a direct bechina relationship found in the source text and confirmed by the Rashi citation.
additions.source_quote: לִוְיָתָן זֶה בְּחִינַת מַלְכוּת, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: לִוְיָתָן נָחָשׁ בָּרִיחַ... וּפֵרֵשׁ רַשִׁ"י: מַלְכוּת

additions.reason: Parnasah (sustenance/livelihood) is the bechina of what flows through malkhut from the yadayim of chokhmah. The Torah uses explicit bechina language for parnasah in multiple places, including: 'le-sachek bo — bechina't shehakim, she-sham shoch'kin man' (shehakim = the heavenly realm where manna is ground = parnasah). Parnasah is closely tied to malkhut/Livyatan in this Torah.
additions.source_quote: הַפַּרְנָסָה... נִשְׁחֶקֶת וְנִכְתֶּשֶׁת אֵצֶל בְּחִינַת הַמַּלְכוּת שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת לִוְיָתָן

additions.reason: Cherut (freedom/liberty) is equated with yovel in the Torah: 'cherut zeh bechina't yovel, she-hu bechina't klaliut ben ve-talmid'. Since yovel is itself the bechina of ben/talmid unity, cherut belongs to the same domain. It is a new node related to the ben/talmid cluster.

additions.reason: The Temple is explicitly called bechina of klaliut ben ve-talmid: 'Beit ha-Mikdash kalul mi-bechinot ben ve-talmid'. It is also called bechina of the goren (threshing floor = parnasah site). The Temple is the structural equivalent of the ben/talmid unity in its highest institutional form.

additions.reason: Chanukah is explicitly called bechina of chanukat ha-bayit (the Temple dedication): 'naaseh bechina't chanukat ha-bayit, bechina't Chanukah, hefekh churban ha-bayit'. Chanukah is structurally the opposite/repair of the Temple's destruction, and is achieved through the 'slach na' prayer. This is a central bechina of the final section of the Torah.
additions.source_quote: כְּשֶׁזָּכָה לִפְעֹל בַּקָּשָׁתוֹ, מִזֶּה נַעֲשֶׂה בְּחִינַת חֲנֻכַּת הַבַּיִת, בְּחִינַת חֲנֻכָּה, הֶפֶךְ חֻרְבַּן הַבַּיִת

additions.reason: The destruction of the Temple is used as the evil mirror of Chanukah in this Torah. The text explicitly pairs churban as the opposite of chanukat ha-bayit, making it the anti-node to the Chanukah concept. In the polarity structure of this Torah, churban is the evil counterpart to the holy restoration concept of Chanukah.

The yadayim (hands) in the sea of chokhmah are the bechina of remezim (hints/allusions) that the chakham gives his students: 'eleh ha-remezim hem bechina't yadayim, bechina't: natiti yadi'. These hands/hints channel parnasah to malkhut. This is a key technical bechina in the Torah's flow from ben/talmid to malkhut/parnasah.

Remezim (hints) are the bechina of yadayim (hands), which are themselves the channel through which parnasah flows from chokhmah to malkhut. The Torah cites Rashi explicitly: 'natiti yadi — hints (remezim)'. The bechina chain: remezim = yadayim = the conduit of sustenance from wisdom.

structural_notes: The dataset for Torah 7 (LM2) is severely incomplete. Of the Torah's most prominent conceptual domains — ben/talmid/makifim/malkhut/parnasah — NONE appear in the dataset edges. Only the secondary domains (emunah/tefilla, Yosef/brit/tzitzit, etzah/nissu'in) are captured.

The ben/talmid cluster and the malkhut/parnasah cluster appear to be the two major conceptual domains that are entirely missing from the dataset. They would form at least 2 new packages if their bechina edges were added.

Packages 7, 8, and 9 in the current proposals are thematically extensions of Package 1 (emunah/tefilla/nisim) and should ideally be merged into it once the missing bechina links are verified in the source text.
All 36 dataset nodes are accounted for in the 11 packages — there are no orphaned nodes from the dataset.
